courses.name: How your mind works
courses.why: Memory, attention, choices and feelings run every day of a person's life, and knowing the rules lets them fool themselves less.
units: What psychology is and is not
Other people: groups, conformity and persuasion

courses.name: Old psychology, still true
courses.why: William James described habit, attention and the stream of thought in plain prose that still beats most modern advice.
units: The self and its many parts
Emotion: do we cry because we are sad

courses.name: Crowds, calm and character
courses.why: People follow crowds, panic and persuasion; ancient and old books give tools for keeping a clear head.
units: What is up to you and what is not
Persuasion and how to spot it
Stress today: what current science says

sources.title: Introduction to Psychology
sources.licenceSeen: Course page footer and oyc.yale.edu/terms section 4 'Course License' (read 2026-11-15)
sources.terms: CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 US: non-commercial only. OYC terms count advertising, paid services, or required email sign-up on the reusing site as commercial use, so check that before use. Credit the professor, Yale and oyc.yale.edu. Third-party content in lecture Credits is not covered. No clause about AI or language models found on the terms page.
coursework: lecture video (YouTube embed on each lecture page)
sources.needIt: A full tour of the mind that makes sense of memory, bias, emotion and other people, for any reader.
sources.notes: 20 lectures plus 2 guest lectures, Spring 2007. Archive item psychologypaulbloom holds 40 mp4 files (about 20 lectures in two encodings) and shows no licence field; the licence is read on oyc.yale.edu. Archive item oyc_Introduction_to_Psychology is the audio set (20 mp3). Some findings (for example priming studies) have not held up; flag them.
